findings.title: a.out symbol reservation omits its leading size word
findings.detail: For Multiboot bit 4, addr points at the leading four-byte symbol-array size, not the first nlist entry. tabsize counts the array; strsize includes the string-section size word. Reserving only tabsize + strsize is four bytes short. This can leave a live final frame available to the frame allocator, and can miss a forbidden-range intersection. For example addr=0x300fc8, tabsize=24, strsize=32 currently reserves through 0x301000, while the actual end is 0x301004. The next frame can then be reused despite owning symbol bytes.
findings.smallest_correction: Reject bit 4 as unsupported, or checked-add the leading four-byte word to the a.out byte span and validate/reserve the whole range. Validate its reserved field if accepting this feature.
findings.test_gap: tests_kernel/src/b18_inventory_tests.rs:487-498 currently expects the short reservation. Correct the oracle, and add a page-boundary tail fixture plus a final-four-byte reserved/kernel/growth intersection case.
findings.verification: Static code inspection, official-spec web-search text, and Python boundary arithmetic; no kernel/test execution.

findings.title: Borrowed backing retains freed frame addresses after failed construction
findings.detail: Partial-exhaustion cleanup frees table frames but leaves their nonzero addresses in caller-owned tables. Reusing the advertised retained backing can make subsequent failure cleanup free frames now owned by another allocation, including a retry's directory, and can double-free the directory. Concrete trace: first attempt with frames A/B allocates directory A and table B then fails, leaving tables[0]=B and freeing both. Another owner allocates A then B. A later attempt allocates a new directory C but has no table frame; cleanup frees stale B despite the other owner still using it. Fresh tables in the existing B26 loop hide this. review_r1_tests explicitly calls tables.fill(0) before retry, masking the production ownership defect.
findings.smallest_correction: On failed build, clear every occupied table slot as it is freed (for example mem::replace(slot, 0)), and ensure cleanup only visits frames owned by this attempt. Document/enforce initially zeroed length-1024 backing, or validate it before allocating the directory.
findings.test_gap: Reuse the identical tables Vec after failure without manually clearing it; interleave unrelated allocations before the retry, then force another failure and assert those owners remain allocated and invalid/double-free counts stay zero.
findings.verification: Static ownership trace only. The production prepare path currently creates fresh backing, so the demonstrated corruption requires reuse of the new in-place builder API.

findings.title: Fallible backing failures are converted into allocating errors
findings.detail: A try_reserve_exact failure is immediately converted with vec![message], which itself allocates. required_regions and validate_mapping also grow Vecs infallibly. Thus actual bootstrap-heap exhaustion after a successfully parsed inventory can still enter alloc_error_handler instead of returning to the promised independent RAMFS recovery path. Unlocking before allocation fixes B26 lock inversion but does not satisfy B18 fallible recovery; the function comment acknowledges this unresolved behavior.
findings.smallest_correction: Return a scalar/static MemoryPrepareError (or bounded fixed diagnostics), propagate it without allocating, and make required-region/mapping validation allocation-free or fully fallible. Alternatively prove and reserve a complete worst-case bootstrap budget before this phase; parser fallibility alone is insufficient.
findings.test_gap: Inject allocator refusal at pin backing, table backing, required-region collection, and missing-diagnostic collection. Verify no fallback error allocation/panic and no published map/live paging frames. Existing B26 instrumentation counts operations under the frame lock; it does not inject heap OOM.
findings.verification: Static control-flow inspection; no allocator fault injection executed.
